agree.reason: Commissioners worried about traffic hear the D rating played down as 'a little longer' and get only a vague timing review, not the builder-funded signal that keeps the intersection at C, so the resisting reader has little reason to change their vote.

honest.reason: The numbers are accurate, but the speech says the project 'would house 64 of them' (waiting-list families), which the facts do not guarantee, and it calls a drop from C to D only 'a little longer' at the light.

works_the_facts.reason: It works out the one-in-six share of the waiting list and the more-than-one-space-per-home parking ratio, but it never sets 64 units against the 2,100-home shortfall and ignores the signal that keeps the C rating.

right_comparison.reason: The 'if you say no' paragraph sets out the status quo fairly (an empty lot, families still waiting, the same traffic), though it skips the existing 8am backups that would make the comparison sharper.

qualification.reason: The only condition is a staff review of signal timing 'once occupied', with no date, no measure and no consequence if the review is missed or the result is bad, and it replaces the signal condition the speaker actually wants.

objections.reason: It takes on rush-hour traffic but answers it weakly, and it leaves out 20 months of construction trucks, the neighbour parking commitment and the neighbour group, which are concerns this room will have.

fit.reason: It reads as a spoken public comment, but at about 480 words it runs slightly past three minutes and still has unfilled placeholders for the name, the church and a parking sentence.
